# `begin_recv`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Updater: open the destination file and begin receiving a firmware/file upload.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, updater begin_recv @0x26e10, prepareRecv @0x28840 and networkThread @0xf150 (64-bit build); 32-bit build carries the same strings; firmware 9.75 begin_recv @0x292e0 and prepareRecv @0x2d490 (64-bit build), 32-bit begin_recv @0x2e5c0; app 3.3.2 DeviceFwFragment.handleVersionEvent emitter |

Updater method on TCP 4350, paired with stop_recv. Params are an object or a one-element array whose element is that object; the handler reads file_name (string), run_update (integer; nonzero is true), file_len (integer) and md5 (string). It validates file_name, creates the target file for writing in the updater's private directory under the device user's home, and arms the caller's own 4361 connection (copying the file record into it, allocating a buffer and timestamping it). A client must open 4361 before sending begin_recv. Success is result 0; the app then streams the raw bytes on 4361. After the transfer the updater checks the file MD5 against md5, then a package signature with a built-in key; either failure ends with a failing Receive state. READ. That file_len is the expected byte count that ends the receive and that run_update gates installation is INFERRED. The app sends run_update as JSON true; that the integer read accepts true is INFERRED (the type test was not traced). Firmware 9.75 (64-bit build, READ; the 32-bit build has the method and the run_update string but no legacy-lock code, INFERRED from absence) types the members strictly. file_len is accepted only as a JSON integer (a float or a string such as 123.0 is ignored and file_len stays 0), file_name and md5 must be strings, and run_update is accepted only as the JSON literal true or false (a numeric 1 is not accepted and the flag stays false). A file_len of 0 or an empty file_name gives error 1 with the text expected param. With run_update true the destination is the legacy update package directory plus file_name and the handler does not open the file itself; with run_update false it is a temporary path and the handler creates the file (258 on failure). The handler validates, then calls the shared receive preparation, which for run_update true takes a non-blocking legacy update lock (524 failed to acquire legacy update lock when held), clears the legacy update directory (257 failed to prepare legacy update directories when that fails), reserves the receive and releases the lock before returning; the lock does not cover the transfer or the install. On any preparation failure a failed update result is recorded and the error is returned.

Side effects: Creates (truncates) the destination file for writing and arms shared receive state on the caller's 4361 connection; a failed arm also records a failed update result. Pairs with stop_recv. The byte transfer itself is over the separate upload channel.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"begin_recv"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | yes | - | The upload descriptor as an object, or a one-element array whose element is that object (the app sends the array form). Missing params give 107; a missing or mistyped member gives 1. [READ] |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | No params object | `expected object param` |
| 1 | A required member is missing or has the wrong type; in firmware 9.75 also file_len of 0 or an empty file_name | `expected param (firmware 9.75; 9.31 text not stated)` |
| 102 | Invalid file_name (leading dot, contains "..", longer than 255 bytes, or characters other than letters, digits, "-" and "_") | `invalid file_name` |
| 258 | The target file cannot be created for writing | `fail to create file` |
| 257 | Firmware 9.75 (64-bit build) the legacy update directories could not be prepared | `failed to prepare legacy update directories` |
| 524 | Cannot arm the receive (no 4361 connection from this client, a receive already running, or an update already running); a failed update result is also recorded | `per cause, e.g. binary port is not connected, receive is already running, is already updating, failed to acquire legacy update lock (firmware 9.75)` |

207 was not seen in this handler; the app special-cases 207 and 524 when displaying an error. MD5 and signature failures are reported later through Receive, not in this reply. Dispatcher rows are not listed.

## Example

Request, request - Shape READ from the app emitter (id 100 is what the app uses); length and digest invented:

```json
{"id":100,"method":"begin_recv","params":[{"file_name":"air","run_update":true,"file_len":1048576,"md5":"<32 hex digits>"}]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"begin_recv","result":0,"code":0,"id":100}
```
